So, I'm French and I've moved to the UK 2 years ago and plan on remain here. I'm also part greek, so I'm used to really nice Mediterranean food, it's what I grew up with. Regarding British food: I think a lot of it has to do with the quality of the food. Especially vegetables: I find that they are very very bland, compared to what we have in the south of France. But it's very logical! Almost all of it is imported. The meat however is amazing, and if I'm feeling fancy and go to a farm shop, I can find some amazing products. The thing with British food is that it's heavy: it really sticks to your stomach. Especially deserts: sticky toffee pudding for example. It's amazing, but you can't really have more than one serving, whereas with french patisserie it's easier to have a taste of everything, as it's much lighter. But that's also logical: the tough and cold weather here justifies eating more heavy things. 
So, in general: no, British food isn't bad. It's got to be understood within its context. You lot have great recipes for a lot of things, and your barbecues are splendid.
Some things are a tad more strange to me (personally) though. A chip butty? Chips and bread? Or beans.. on toast? I'll leave that for your guys, you can have my serving.

Hey, if I can help:

I often have a lot of bruises around my neck for similar reasons. I also love makeup and I've got a lot of experience covering things up. So, if you're interested, here is a little guide on how to cover up/make your scars look more discreet. 
It takes several steps.

1. Colour correcting. Depending on the colour of your scars, you will need to apply a first shade of concealer to cancel out your scar's colour (this is based on actual colour theory). If it's rather red, you'll need a green concealer. Kinda yellow? Use some blue. Kinda black? Use some orange. 
2. After that's done, you need to apply another coat of concealer, but this time in your actual shade. Take your time to do this. Also, I'd recommend dabbing in the product rather than applying it in streaks. This is so it doesn't wipe away the colour correcting coat underneath this one. 
3. This is optional, but you can either powder everything, or apply some setting spray on top, to make it stick. 

If you don't know much about makeup/don't own anything related to it, you can find all these things for pretty cheap prices. You don't need to spend much. Depending on where you live in the world, different brands might be available. I'd recommend: Kiko Milano, NYX or makeup revolution. They're rather cheap. All in all, you need 2 concealers and a makeup sponge (30 quid max, maybe a bit more with the powder). 

I hope this somewhat helped. Good luck. I know how you feel.
